summary: You take the core courses, a grant writing course and 10 units of electives (a biochemistry course, an advanced genetics, genomics or cell biology course, and science electives), each letter graded where offered with a B or better, toward 45 units. The MS is awarded after the PhD's first two years, so the lab rotations, the qualifying exam and the 20-page research report the Director of Graduate Studies approves are checked by hand.

program.why: Grading: "All required courses, including those counting toward the 10 units of elective credit, must be taken for a letter grade if offered and must be passed with a B grade or better."

HjC23Gpc.why: "Complete 10 units from the following areas." Block notes: "Students must take upper-division elective units relevant to the dissertation and career goals, totaling at least ten units." The three numbered areas (Elective 1, 2, 3) each stay one course.

node.name: Three one-quarter laboratory rotations in the first year

add.why: "each student must complete three one-quarter laboratory rotations during the first year. All rotations must be approved by the DGS, Executive Director and SSO prior to the start of the rotation. Two rotations (including the first rotation) must be done with ISCBRM faculty."
"Students in the PhD program may apply for an MS degree after satisfactorily completing the course and laboratory requirements of the first two years, including the qualifying exam."

node.name: 20-page research report (NIH format) approved by the Director of Graduate Studies

add.why: Learning Outcomes tab: "Students wishing to do so must have completed 45 academic units of study and submit a scholarly 20-page research report (standard NIH format). This report must meet a sufficient scholarly standard as judged by the Director of Graduate Studies."
